issues.description: The problem statement instructs that the SealSaloon 'stock' attribute should be shared across all instances (static) but also says 'These should be initialized to default values ... in the constructor of SealSaloon'. This is contradictory: a static (shared) attribute is not typically initialized in an instance constructor. The solution initializes the static stock at the field declaration (private static final Stock stock = new Stock()), which conflicts with the earlier instruction to initialize it in the constructor and may confuse students about where and how to initialize the shared stock.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the specification: state that 'stock' must be a static (class-level) attribute and show the recommended initialization (either at declaration or in a static initializer). Explicitly instruct students to initialize instance fields like 'orders' in the constructor, and to initialize the shared 'stock' at declaration (e.g., private static final Stock stock = new Stock();) or in a static initializer block.

issues.description: The UML and problem description list a method named checkOrderReady() that should be implemented and called after ordering. The solution implementation instead provides a method named processOrders() and orderMeal() calls processOrders(). This name/signature mismatch between the described API (checkOrderReady) and the reference implementation (processOrders) can confuse students about the required method name specified in the exercise and in any tests or UML diagrams.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either rename processOrders() in the solution to checkOrderReady(), or update the problem statement and UML to refer to processOrders(). Additionally, ensure the API described in the problem (method names and signatures) matches the reference implementation so students clearly know which method to implement.

issues.description: The problem statement requires a method named checkOrderReady() on SealSaloon (used by orderMeal and described in the UML and text). The provided solution implementation instead exposes a method named processOrders() that implements the described behaviour and is invoked by orderMeal. This name divergence (checkOrderReady vs processOrders) breaks direct mapping between the exercise requirements and the implementation students will see as a reference, increasing cognitive load and risking confusion about which method to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the solution method processOrders() to checkOrderReady() (and keep its behaviour), and have orderMeal call checkOrderReady(). Alternatively, provide a small wrapper method checkOrderReady() that delegates to processOrders() so the API matches the problem statement and UML.
